info.title: ai-service
info.description:
Standalone, project-agnostic AI + RAG service. Consumed over HTTP by multiple applications. See `@edc/ai-client` for the typed client.

This document is DERIVED: every request and response shape in it comes from the Zod schemas in `src/contract/`, which are the same schemas the service gates on at runtime. Nothing here is restated by hand, so it cannot drift from the service.

Bearer.description: Per-project bearer token. Resolves the caller to a {org, project} scope; every row is stamped with both. A key configured with a delegation prefix may also send `X-AI-Org: <suffix>` (suffix ^[a-z0-9-]{1,48}$) to act as org `<prefix><suffix>`: budget, usage and corpora then belong to that org. The header on a key without a prefix is 403 org_delegation_forbidden; an invalid suffix is 400 invalid_org. Capability: orgDelegation.

responseSchemaStrict.description: Strict schema-constrained output. `true` asks the provider for `response_format: json_schema` with `strict: true`, so decoding is constrained to `responseSchema` (JSON mode only promises valid JSON, and accepts a model that echoes the schema back). Needs a `responseSchema` inside the strict subset (every object has `additionalProperties: false` and lists every property in `required`; no `minLength`, `allOf`, `default`, …) and a model listed in `GET /v1/capabilities` `strictStructuredOutputModels`. Otherwise 400 `SpecResolutionError` with cause `strict schema unsupported model` or `strict schema invalid`; never a silent fall back to JSON mode. Absent or false: JSON mode, as before. Applies to whichever layer supplied the schema, a registry row included.

get.summary: Named capabilities this deployment ships (ADR-0004).
get.description: Consumers declare the capabilities they require and negotiate at boot, so a wrong promotion order fails at deploy time with an actionable message instead of silently degrading (service ahead of consumer) or throwing mid-user-action (consumer ahead of service). Compatibility is decided on capability NAMES only — the document deliberately carries no version or build id. Unauthenticated: a consumer must be able to tell a missing capability apart from a bad API key. Also outside the rate limiter, for the same reason.

401.description: Missing, unknown or expired bearer token. `error` is `unauthorized` or `api_key_expired`; the two are distinguished so a consumer can tell a rotation it has to act on from a token it never had.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. 100 requests/minute across `/v1`, 30/minute on the three `/v1/generate*` POSTs and `/v1/retrieve/multi`, bucketed by API key (never by IP — `trustProxy` makes that caller-controlled). `retryAfterMs` mirrors the `retry-after` header in milliseconds. The limiter FAILS OPEN: while its Redis store is unreachable nothing is counted and no 429 is sent, so absence of a 429 is not proof you are under the cap.

post.summary: Enqueue a batch of generation units.
post.description: Returns as soon as the work is queued; follow it on `GET /v1/events/{channel}` using the `channel` in the response. Sending the same `clientRequestId` twice REPLAYS the stored handle — that reply carries the four required fields and never `warnings`, because the warning belonged to the original call.

400.description: THREE producers, and they do NOT share an envelope. (1) Request-body validation → `{statusCode, error, message}`. (2) `RenderError`, `SpecResolutionError`, `DependencyCycleError`, `CrossBatchDependencyError` → the flat `{error, message}`, NO `statusCode` and NO `code`. (3) `CallbackUrlBlockedError` → the flat envelope PLUS `code: "ERR_CALLBACK_URL_BLOCKED"`. Branch on the presence of `statusCode` first, then on `error`.

post.summary: One generation, streamed as Server-Sent Events.
post.description:
The reply is HIJACKED once the first byte is written, which changes what a failure looks like. Everything up to that point (validation, spec resolution, context fetch) can still answer with a normal status. After it, the status line is already `200` and every failure — INCLUDING a budget refusal that would be a 402 on `/sync`, and an open circuit breaker that would be a 503 — arrives as a terminal `error` FRAME.

**Framing.** `text/event-stream`. The stream opens with the comment frame `: ok`, then every payload is one `data: <json>` frame. Three frame types, discriminated on `type`:

- `delta` — an incremental text batch. ZERO of these on a cache hit.
- `done` — terminal success. Field-for-field the `/v1/generate/sync` 200 body, plus `type`.
- `error` — terminal failure.

⚠ **The error field names swap between transports.** On this route `code` is what the JSON body calls `error` (the class discriminator) and `errorCode` is what the JSON body calls `code` (the `ERR_*` string). A consumer sharing one error mapper across `/sync` and `/stream` must translate. Only classes marked mid-stream-reachable name themselves; anything else collapses to `INTERNAL` / `generation failed`.

200.description: The stream. Frames are `delta`* then exactly one of `done` or `error`.

400.description: Raised BEFORE the hijack, so it still has a status line. Validation → `{statusCode, error, message}`; `SpecResolutionError` / `RenderError` → the flat `{error, message}`, no `statusCode`.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream for one generation request.
get.description:
Channel format: `request:<requestId>:generations`. Cross-tenant subscription is rejected with 403 BEFORE any byte hits the wire, which is why it can still be a status rather than a frame.

**Framing.** Opens with the comment frame `: ok`, then a `: ping` comment every 15 s to stop intermediaries reaping an idle connection. Payloads are `data: <json>`, each one generation event for THIS request. There is no terminal frame — the stream simply ends.

post.description:
Text-only: the service does not parse PDFs or HTML. Documents are chunked, embedded and indexed asynchronously; poll `GET /v1/ingest/{ingestId}` or supply `callbackUrl`.

**Chunking.** By default a document is split by the corpus's configured strategy (`recursive-char`, a token window). Send `chunkConfig` — at the batch level, or per document, where the per-document value wins — to split at the document's OWN headings instead, so a retrieved chunk corresponds to one addressable, citable unit:

```json
{
  "sections": [{ "key": "section", "pattern": "^\\s*Section\\s+(\\d+)\\b", "flags": "i" }],
  "subSections": [{ "key": "clause", "pattern": "^\\s*([IVX]+)[.)]\\s" }]
}
```

`pattern` is JS regex source with `gm` forced on; capture group 1 is the identifier, stored on each chunk as `metadata[key]` (under your own document metadata, which always wins a key collision). `sections` is the only required field; `maxChars` (default 4000) and `minChars` (default 80) are optional. The service ships NO named presets — the patterns describe your documents, so you own them. An unusable config, or one that matches no boundary in a given document, falls back to the corpus strategy with a warning rather than failing the ingest.

post.summary: Top-K retrieval over a corpus — dense, or hybrid dense+lexical (RRF).
post.description:
Cosine top-K over the corpus embedding index, with optional MMR rerank. Every parameter beyond `corpus` and `query` is additive: omitting all of them reproduces the original behaviour exactly.

- `filter` — jsonb-containment constraint on chunk metadata, applied before ranking.
- `asOf` — point-in-time constraint. Only chunks whose `[validFrom, validTo)` interval contains this instant are eligible. Chunks with no bounds are always eligible, so this is a no-op on a corpus that never sets validity. Use it together with the `validFrom`/`validTo` fields on ingest to keep superseded content out of the candidate set entirely, rather than filtering it at display time.
- `mode: "hybrid"` — additionally runs a Postgres full-text leg and fuses it with the dense leg via Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Fixes exact-identifier queries (codes, numbered references, other short literal tokens) that dense embeddings systematically miss. **In hybrid mode `score` is an RRF score, not a cosine similarity** — read `denseScore` if you threshold on it.
- `rerank: true` — re-score a capped top-N pool with a cross-encoder (self-hosted `bge-reranker-v2-m3`) after retrieval, then re-order before the final top-K, surfacing `rerankScore`. A NO-OP unless the server has rerank wired (`RERANK_ENABLED` + `RERANK_URL`), and it fails safe to the un-reranked order on any rerank error/timeout. Mutually exclusive with `mmr` (rerank wins). **When rerank is on, `score` is the cross-encoder score (0–1 sigmoid)** — threshold on `rerankScore`, not `denseScore`.
- `rerankModel` — per-request rerank model override. Only used when `rerank` is set, but always checked: when the server's rerank provider is `deepinfra`, a model outside its rerank allowlist is a **400**, even when `rerank` is absent or false.

`legs` names the retrieval legs that returned CANDIDATE rows, which is the only way to tell a degraded retrieve from a normal one: because the rerank rung fails safe, a response from a DOWN reranker is otherwise byte-identical to `rerank: false` minus `rerankScore`. It is not a list of the legs whose rows survived into `chunks`, and the unit differs by leg: `dense`, `lexical` and `sparse` count rows returned into the fusion POOL (before RRF and before the final top-K slice), while `rerank` counts rows in the RESPONSE. `topK: 1` on a hybrid retrieve whose lexical leg returned 50 rows that all lost the fusion still reports `[dense, lexical]` next to one dense chunk — a leg is alive when it produces candidates, and whether they win slots is ranking, not health. The two lexical legs are named apart there (`lexical` = Postgres full-text, `sparse` = learned-sparse bge-m3) even though both still fill `lexicalScore`. Read it as a SET — today a hybrid retrieve runs dense plus exactly ONE lexical leg, but the declared next change fuses all three, so never key on its length or index. Absent ⇒ the deployment predates the field; gate on the `retrievalLegs` capability, never on the field itself. This route only — `POST /v1/retrieve/multi` returns no `legs`.

Passage text, GUARANTEED by ai-service to be at most the corpus's own chunk-size contract in characters: `chunk_size` tokens x 4 chars/token (3200 for the default `chunk_size` of 800). The same bound the ingester splits on, so consumers do NOT need to re-trim defensively. A stored chunk that exceeds it (a legacy or hand-inserted row) is truncated to exactly the bound and logged server-side as an anomaly.

legs.description: The legs that returned CANDIDATE rows — not the legs requested, and not the legs whose rows survived into `chunks`. The unit differs by leg: `dense`, `lexical` and `sparse` count rows returned into the fusion POOL, before RRF and before the final top-K slice, while `rerank` counts rows in the RESPONSE. So `topK: 1` on a hybrid retrieve whose lexical leg returned 50 rows that all lost the fusion still reports `[dense, lexical]` alongside one dense chunk. Pool contribution is the liveness signal: a leg is alive when it produces candidates; whether they win slots is ranking, not health. `rerank` appears ONLY when the cross-encoder really scored rows; the rerank rung is fail-safe, so a timeout or a down reranker returns the fused order and omits `rerank` here. Read it as a SET: today a hybrid retrieve runs dense plus exactly ONE lexical leg (`SPARSE_ENABLED` picks which), so `[dense, lexical]` and `[dense, sparse]` are the shapes you see — plus `rerank` when the cross-encoder scored rows, and minus any leg that returned zero rows, which is the very case this field exposes. The declared next change fuses all three, so never key on length or index. OPTIONAL on the wire only because an OLDER deployment omits it entirely; a build that advertises the `retrievalLegs` capability always sends it. Check the capability, not the field, to decide whether absence means "no legs ran" (it never does) or "old service". Single-corpus only: `POST /v1/retrieve/multi` returns no `legs` at all, so nothing here describes that route.

post.summary: Fan out retrieval across N corpora, fuse across them, optional query rewrite.
post.description:
Runs `/v1/retrieve` against every `corpora[]` name in parallel (all under the caller's own `(org, project)`), merges the matches by `score`, dedupes by chunk, caps at `limit`, and tags each returned chunk with the `corpus` it came from. Every per-corpus knob (`mmr`, `mode`, `rrfK`, `filter`, `asOf`) is forwarded unchanged.

- A missing or erroring corpus never fails the whole call: it contributes no chunks and is recorded in the `corpora` diagnostics of the response. That is why this route has no 404.
- `rewrite` (optional) condenses an anaphoric follow-up into a standalone query using the supplied conversation `history` and the cheapest LLM tier BEFORE fan-out. The service ships no prompt wording — `rewrite.instruction` carries all of it (locale included). It fails safe to the raw `query` on the first turn or any error. `query` in the response is the query actually used, and `rewritten` says whether it changed.
- `rerank: true` (optional) re-scores a capped top-N pool with a cross-encoder (self-hosted `bge-reranker-v2-m3`) **once, AFTER cross-corpus fusion** — not per corpus — then re-orders before the final `limit`, surfacing `rerankScore`. The reranked pool spans multiple corpora, which is fine: a cross-encoder scores each (query, chunk) pair independently of its source, and `corpus` provenance is preserved. A NO-OP unless the server has rerank wired (`RERANK_ENABLED` + `RERANK_URL`), and it fails safe to the fused order on any rerank error/timeout. Mutually exclusive with `mmr` (rerank wins; `mmr` is not forwarded to the legs). **When rerank is on, `score` is the cross-encoder score (0–1 sigmoid)** — threshold on `rerankScore`, not `denseScore`.
- `rerankModel` — per-request rerank model override. Only used when `rerank` is set, but always checked: when the server's rerank provider is `deepinfra`, a model outside its rerank allowlist is a **400**, even when `rerank` is absent or false.
- **Cross-corpus fusion.** In `mode: 'hybrid'` each corpus returns `score` as an RRF value built from RANKS INSIDE THAT CORPUS'S OWN pool, and those are not comparable across corpora — a deeper corpus is penalised for its depth. (MEASURED on dev 2026-09-17: a 180-chunk corpus whose best chunk had the higher lexical scores lost every slot to a 10-chunk corpus, because all of the small corpus's hits sat at ranks 1–8 of a 10-deep pool.) So for hybrid over MORE THAN ONE corpus this route rebuilds the ranks over one global pool per leg and re-runs RRF; `score` is then that global RRF value, on the same scale as before. A single corpus, and `mode: 'dense'` (where `score` is cosine and already comparable), keep the plain score sort unchanged. `fusion` in the response says which rule ran.
- **Fusion diagnostics.** `corpora[].matched` is what a corpus FOUND; `corpora[].contributed` is how many of its chunks won a slot in the final `chunks`. `matched: 8, contributed: 0` is a corpus that was indexed, queried and matched and still reached you with nothing — check it before concluding an attachment had no relevant text. The server also logs that case.
- This response carries NO `legs` field; that is `/v1/retrieve` only. So a rerank rung that failed safe here is still indistinguishable from `rerank: false`, and a dead leg inside any single corpus is still invisible.

Passage text, GUARANTEED by ai-service to be at most the corpus's own chunk-size contract in characters: `chunk_size` tokens x 4 chars/token (3200 for the default `chunk_size` of 800). The same bound the ingester splits on, so consumers do NOT need to re-trim defensively. A stored chunk that exceeds it (a legacy or hand-inserted row) is truncated to exactly the bound and logged server-side as an anomaly.

post.summary: Classify a question onto exactly one caller-supplied candidate id.
post.description: Single cheap LLM classification over a GENERIC candidate list. FAIL-SAFE: any error / ambiguity / invalid routeId returns `defaultRouteId` (else `candidates[0].id`) with an explanatory reason — never a 5xx on a routable request — except the provider TIMEOUT, which is a 504 `ProviderTimeout` (unbilled, `truncated: true`), never a fallback. The chosen `routeId` is always one of the supplied candidate ids. Because of that, **a degraded answer and a real one are both 200**. Tell them apart by `fallback` (`true` ⇒ default route, with `fallbackCause`), or by `reason` starting with `fallback:` on servers older than 2026-10-06. Every fallback is also logged and counted (`ai_route_fallback_total{cause}`). Override the router prompt/model/effort by registering the `capability-router` unit-type in the registry: a registered entry WINS over the built-in prompt, which is only the fallback used when no entry exists. Model precedence, highest first: request `modelOverride`, the registered `model`, its `effortProfiles[level].model`, `project_configs.defaultModel`, `project_configs.effortProfiles[level].model`, then the tier default (`openai/gpt-4o-mini` for `quick`, the router's default tier).

reason.description: `fallback: …` ⇒ the default route was used, not a model choice.

fallback.description: True ⇒ the default route was used, not a model choice. Sent on every 200 since 2026-10-06.

fallbackCause.description: Why the router degraded (only with `fallback: true`): `router_call_failed` (provider error, budget refusal, bad spec), `router_unparseable` (no `routeId` readable), `router_invalid_route` (an id that was not offered).

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. 100 requests/minute across `/v1`, 30/minute on the three `/v1/generate*` POSTs and `/v1/retrieve/multi`, bucketed by API key (never by IP — `trustProxy` makes that caller-controlled). `retryAfterMs` mirrors the `retry-after` header in milliseconds. patch.summary: Reconfigure a corpus (chunking, language, metadata; model only while empty).
patch.description: App-role bearer token. Only the fields present in the body change. Changing `language` RE-INDEXES the corpus: the stored lexical tsvectors are rebuilt with the new text-search config in the same transaction as the config write, so the index and the query side cannot drift apart. Vectors are untouched (no re-embedding, no token cost) and dense retrieval is unaffected. Sending the language it already has is a no-op. `embeddingModel` may change ONLY while the corpus is still empty — otherwise 409 `EMBEDDING_MODEL_LOCKED`, because re-embedding existing vectors is a separate, future operation.

400.description: Validation error or an empty patch → `{statusCode, error, message}`. Model↔dimension mismatch (`ERR_EMBEDDING_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`) or an unknown Postgres text-search config (`ERR_INVALID_TEXT_SEARCH_CONFIG`) → the coded flat envelope.

409.description: TWO codes, not one. `EMBEDDING_MODEL_LOCKED` — a model change on a corpus that already has chunks. `CHUNK_SIZE_LOCKED` — lowering `chunkSize` on a corpus that already has chunks; the old and new sizes appear only inside `message`, never as fields.

post.summary: Create or repoint a corpus alias (a cheap, re-embed-free pointer).
post.description: Admin role required. Makes the alias `{name}` resolve to the same chunks as `target` WITHOUT re-embedding — the `:latest`-pointer use-case. Scoped to the caller's (org, project): the target must be in the same tenant, and an alias name cannot collide with a real corpus name. If the target corpus is later deleted, the alias is removed (FK cascade) and a retrieve via it 404s.

patch.summary: Set or clear a document's temporal validity — no re-embedding.
patch.description:
Rewrites the `[validFrom, validTo)` bounds on an ingested document and every chunk it owns, in one transaction, WITHOUT touching embeddings. This is how a consumer retires superseded content: supersession is normally discovered after ingest, and the alternative — re-POSTing the full text to `/v1/ingest` just to write two timestamps — would re-chunk and re-embed the whole document. That cost is what tempts a consumer to skip the step and leave stale content retrievable.

`null` CLEARS a bound (back to unbounded); OMITTING a field leaves the stored bound untouched — the distinction is what makes un-retiring expressible. At least one field must be present.

App role, scoped to the caller's (org, project) — same posture as the DELETE routes. Retrieval honours the bounds via the `asOf` parameter on `/v1/retrieve`.
